turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the device physics

**What the training set says about "what wins" in n‑i‑p MAPbI₃:**

1. **The best-performing ETLs are bilayers that combine a compact oxide with a second, better band-aligned / passivating layer.** The single highest entry (20.85 %) is `TiO2-c | SnO2-np` + Spiro; SnO₂ has a deeper, more favourable CBM than TiO₂ and far fewer surface trap states/less UV photocatalytic damage, so the electron extraction barrier and interfacial recombination at the ETL/MAPbI₃ junction both drop → high FF and V_OC.
2. **Fullerene interlayers on the oxide** (`TiO2-c | C60` 17.2, `TiO2-c | PCBM-60` 14–17, `SnO2-c | PCBM-60` 17.3–18.0, `TiO2-c | PCBM-60 | C60-ETA` 16.9) passivate the oxide surface and grain boundaries at the buried interface, systematically pushing devices to 16–19 %.
3. **The HTL matters mostly through selectivity and doping stability**: doped Spiro‑MeOTAD, PTAA, and well-matched donor polymers (PCDTBT-type, 19.35 %) are the top tier; P3HT, phthalocyanines, small-molecule "novel" HTMs and HTL-free carbon stacks sit lower (5–15 %).
4. **Fully evaporated p‑i‑n-style doped-organic contacts (TaTm/F6‑TCNNQ with C60:PhIm)** reach 17.9 % in the training set — pinhole-free, dopant-graded contacts give excellent FF.
5. **Penalties**: flexible PEN/PET/AZO substrates (higher sheet resistance, lower-T processing), mesoporous-only or HTL-free carbon stacks, ZnO ETLs (chemical degradation of MAPbI₃ at the interface), and "none"/exotic back contacts.

**Applying this to the pool:**

- **c064** `TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro‑MeOTAD / Au` on rigid FTO — the exact winning ETL bilayer of the 20.85 % record, with the best HTL and an inert high-work-function Au contact. Best band alignment + lowest interface recombination in the pool.
- **c005** `TiO2-c | PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3|Au` — fullerene-passivated buried interface plus a deep-HOMO conjugated-polymer HTL with a MoO₃ hole-injection buffer; the direct analogue (PCDTBT1) is the 19.35 % training entry.
- **c017** `C60;PhIm | C60 / TaTm | F6‑TCNNQ:TaTm / Ag`, all co-evaporated — the 17.9 % vacuum-processed doped-contact architecture; conformal, dopant-graded, essentially shunt-free.
- **c068** `SnO2-np | TiO2-np / PTAA / Au|MoO3` — SnO₂-based electron contact with PTAA (clean, hysteresis-free, chemically inert interface); PTAA + SnO₂ gives 18.19 % in training, MoO₃ improves hole extraction into Au.
- **c080** `TiO2-c | MPMIC60 / Spiro‑MeOTAD / Ag` — fullerene-derivative monolayer on compact TiO₂: trap passivation and reduced interfacial recombination, the same motif that yields 17.2 % for `TiO2-c | C60`.

(Close runners-up: c073 TiO₂-c|C60/PTAA, c021 SnO₂-np|CPTA, c031 SnO₂/TiO₂ triple oxide — good physics but flexible substrate or a slightly less selective contact.)

**Final: c064, c005, c017, c068, c080**
